Quick read of the attachments + prod logs: two observations so far.

1) Eviction storm on the prefix store. The pinned-prefix map for Sentri’s tenant shows unusually high churn — keys are being evicted and re-inserted within sub-second windows. That triggers additional KV lookups and repeated partial batches which then cause head-of-line blocking when the batch lane for pinned keys is waiting for the KV miss resolution.

2) A batch-routing tweak we deployed yesterday aimed at improving CPU packing appears to treat Sentri’s high-cardinality prefixes as low-priority for hot-lane servicing. Combined with the eviction churn this yields lane starvation and the throughput collapse you’re seeing.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered by speed/risk):
- Option A (fast, low-risk): disable the new batch-routing tweak for the Sentri tenant and force hot-lane servicing for pinned prefixes. This is a dynamic config change, can push in ~10–15m.
- Option B (moderate): temporarily increase prefix store size + TTL for Sentri to reduce evictions. Requires a quick config push and testing (~30–45m).
- Option C (safer but slower): provision a small dedicated pool for Sentri’s route and migrate traffic (requires exec approval for capacity bump, ~2–4 hours).

I’m attaching the eviction log snippet (kv-eviction-log-0418.csv) and a short trace for the lane stalls.

If we want to pursue A, I can coordinate the change with rollout and smoke tests.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: sudden p99 latency and token errors (us-west)

Confirmed with ops: we see eviction churn correlated with a spike in cross-tenant cache pressure between 08:45–08:58 PT. The runtime’s kernel selector promoted a quantized variant for certain shards which reduced memory headroom and pushed eviction rates up.

Proposed technical plan:
1) Apply Ben’s Option A immediately for Sentri (disable routing tweak + pin hot-lane servicing).
2) Run a targeted TTL bump (Option B) to stabilize while we watch metrics for 60m.
3) If we still see >1.5x baseline p99 after 60m, escalate to the dedicated pool plan (Option C) — Jon or I will request capacity from infra.

Risks & notes: Option A should restore throughput rapidly but is a mitigation, not a long-term fix. The quantized-variant promotion seems environment-dependent; we should add a safety rule to the kernel selector to avoid promoting memory-heavy variants for tenants with pinned-prefix patterns.

I’ll start the Option A change now (will update when rolled).

—Jonas
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Subject: Exec sync: SentriHealth priority — KV eviction-induced lane starvation (need approval for temporary capacity bump)

Marissa / Execs —

Summary: SentriHealth is experiencing a production impact (p99 spike, throughput falloff, token error rate ~3%) caused by a combination of: (a) config change to batch-routing deployed yesterday, and (b) an environment-triggered promotion of a quantized variant that reduced available cache headroom. The result: eviction churn of pinned prefixes, head-of-line blocking, and batch-lane starvation.

Immediate mitigation taken: Jonas/Ben applied a dynamic rollback of the batch-routing tweak for Sentri and forced hot-lane servicing for pinned prefixes (Option A). We also bumped TTL for pinned prefixes (temporary). Early telemetry shows p95 improving but p99 still elevated vs baseline by ~1.4x.

Request: we recommend approving a temporary dedicated capacity bump (Option C, small pool for Sentri) to remove the tenant from noisy multi-tenant pressure while we validate a kernel-selector fix and permanent config tuning. The bump would be for 24–48 hours; cost estimate attached (proposed-bump-estimate.pdf).

Customer impact: Sentri has asked for an ETA for full remediation and an SLA credit if we don’t hit p99 targets in the next 4 hours.

Recommendation: approve the bump (I’ll coordinate procurement/infra changes). If execs prefer a lower-cost route, we can extend TTL and keep monitoring for 24h, but this carries residual risk of repeat thrash.

—Stephanie
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
